title: Reaching the interpreter after capture
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be one of its work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $T$ be a natural number. If the configuration of $M$ after $T$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$ is halted, then there is a time $t\le T+1$ at which the capture machine, started on $x$, is in the interpreter-entry configuration associated with that time-$T$ configuration.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
the base machine's configuration after $T$ steps is halted
replaced:
If the base machine halts on input $x$ within $T$ steps, then for some
$t \le T + 1$, running the capture wrapper $t$ steps from its initial
configuration on $x$ reaches the interpreter-entry configuration for the base
machine's configuration at time $T$; since halting is absorbing, all fields of
that configuration --- including the parked input head --- are retained, not
merely the completed output.
